name: Pregnenolone
summary: A steroid the body turns into other hormones and brain-active neurosteroids, sold as a supplement and studied in small trials for pain, schizophrenia and bipolar depression.
what_it_is: Pregnenolone is a neurosteroid, a steroid made in the body that is converted into other steroid hormones and into brain-active steroids such as allopregnanolone. In the US it is sold over the counter as a dietary supplement. Small trials have tested it as an add-on treatment for schizophrenia, bipolar depression and chronic low back pain.

evidence.why: A handful of small randomized trials, each with about 100 people or fewer and lasting 4 to 12 weeks, show mixed benefits for back pain, schizophrenia symptoms and bipolar depression.

status_us.label: Supplement; FDA reviewing it for compounding
status_us.note: Pregnenolone is sold over the counter as a dietary supplement, which FDA does not approve for safety or effectiveness before sale. FDA also lists it in Category 1 (under evaluation) for pharmacy compounding, so pharmacies may compound it while FDA decides.

benefits.claim: Less low back pain, and less pain interference with work and activity, than placebo over 4 weeks in a trial of 94 US veterans
Fewer negative symptoms (blunted emotion, low motivation, loss of pleasure) when added to antipsychotics in an 8-week trial of 60 people with recent-onset schizophrenia

Better depression scores over time on a clinician-rated scale, and higher remission on a self-report scale (61% versus 37%), when added to usual treatment in 80 adults with bipolar depression; the two scales did not agree
Better attention, working memory or verbal memory in small pilot trials in schizophrenia

risks.risk: Mild restlessness, cold hands and feet, muscle pain or stiffness and headache, reported more often than with placebo in earlier trials
Can raise levels of other steroids made from it, so trials excluded people with prostate, uterine or breast cancer
Long-term safety unknown: trials lasted 4 to 12 weeks

avoid_if: Prostate, uterine or breast cancer (excluded from trials because downstream hormones could rise)
interactions: Birth control pills and other hormone supplements: users were excluded from trials, so combined effects are unknown

labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for supplement use; trials measured neurosteroid levels for research, and one planned a follow-up ECG because of a single palpitations report.

studies.title: Effect of Pregnenolone vs Placebo on Self-reported Chronic Low Back Pain Among US Military Veterans: A Randomized Clinical Trial
studies.people: 94 US veterans with chronic low back pain (4 weeks)
studies.finding: Pregnenolone lowered daily pain ratings and pain interference with work and activity more than placebo and was well tolerated.

studies.title: Pregnenolone treatment reduces severity of negative symptoms in recent-onset schizophrenia: an 8-week, double-blind, randomized add-on two-center trial
studies.people: 60 people with recent-onset schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder (8 weeks)
studies.finding: Added to antipsychotics, pregnenolone reduced negative symptoms versus placebo, mainly in people not taking mood stabilizers; other symptoms and functioning did not change.

studies.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Pregnenolone for Bipolar Depression
studies.finding: Clinician-rated depression improved more over time with pregnenolone and self-rated remission was higher, but the two depression scales gave different results; it was well tolerated.

studies.title: Pregnenolone as a novel therapeutic candidate in schizophrenia: emerging preclinical and clinical evidence
studies.people: Animal studies and pilot trials in schizophrenia
studies.finding: Early pilot trials suggested pregnenolone may reduce negative symptoms and improve some cognitive measures; the authors call for larger studies.

ask_your_clinician: Could pregnenolone raise my other hormone levels, given my health history?
Is there evidence for my specific condition, and how would we tell whether it is helping?
Does it interact with my birth control or other hormones?

notes_for_editor: US supplement status and the side-effect list come from a 2015 VA trial protocol, not from FDA or NIH pages; the side effects summarize earlier trials rather than the trial reports themselves. Several trials come from one VA research group. Most papers were read as abstracts; the low back pain abstract gives 94 participants but lists 48 and 52 per group. A 2010 trial of pregnenolone and DHEA in schizophrenia (Journal of Clinical Psychiatry) could not be opened.
